sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast episode 149, recorded on September 25th, 2023.

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we are back from the Slovenia 2023 road trip, and record for the first time in almost four months,
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起，我们刚结束 2023 年斯洛文尼亚公路旅行回来，这是近四个月来我们首次录制节目，

sentences.en: we chat about my new obsession with citystrides.com and more.

sentences.en: This is for clarity for those that are not steeped in the C++ lore conference world.
sentences.zh: 为了让那些不太了解 C++ 会议圈子的人听得更明白，我解释一下。

sentences.en: Hannah Dusakova of CTRE fame, that is Compile Time Regular Expressions.
sentences.zh: Hannah Dusakova，以 CTRE（编译期正则表达式）闻名。

sentences.en: And I've seen she's actually been giving some...
sentences.zh: 我看到她最近一直在做……

sentences.en: I saw her give a talk.
sentences.zh: 我看了她的一次演讲。

sentences.en: I can't remember if it was at C++ on C, or it was some other...
sentences.zh: 我不记得是在 C++ on Sea 还是其他什么地方了……

sentences.en: I don't think it was C++ on C, actually, because I don't recall seeing her there.
sentences.zh: 我觉得应该不是 C++ on Sea，因为我不记得在那里见过她。

sentences.en: But she gave a talk.
sentences.zh: 但她确实做了一次演讲。

sentences.en: I can't remember if it was on coroutines or modules.
sentences.zh: 我不记得是关于协程还是模块的了。

sentences.en: It was some C++ 20.
sentences.zh: 是关于 C++ 20 的一些内容。

sentences.en: She was showing me some of the stuff she's doing with coroutines right now.
sentences.zh: 她当时向我展示了她目前用协程做的一些东西。

sentences.en: She wrote a library called CoCurl, like Curl, the command line tool for accessing a website and downloading stuff from a website.
sentences.zh: 她写了一个叫 CoCurl 的库，就像 Curl 一样，那个用于访问网站和下载内容的命令行工具。

sentences.en: So she wrote a C++ wrapper around Curl that is coroutine, that's based on coroutines.
sentences.zh: 所以她写了一个基于协程的 C++ Curl 封装库。

sentences.en: It has a coroutine interface for managing asynchrony.
sentences.zh: 它有一个用于管理异步的协程接口。

sentences.en: And it's super, super cool and very slick.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常非常酷，而且非常简洁。

sentences.en: And she was showing me how it worked.
sentences.zh: 她当时向我展示了它是如何工作的。

sentences.en: And it does some very clever, clever things.
sentences.zh: 它做了一些非常聪明、非常巧妙的事情。

sentences.en: She actually inspired a secret curroutine project that I'm working on that I can't talk about right now, but it's also very cool.
sentences.zh: 她实际上启发了我正在进行的一个秘密协程项目，我现在还不能说，但它也非常酷。

sentences.en: And I actually just did some interesting stuff with my secret curroutine project today.
sentences.zh: 而且我今天刚在我的秘密协程项目上做了一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: But yeah, she's given that talk, I think, at a meetup in the Czech Republic.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，我想她是在捷克共和国的一个聚会上做的那个演讲。

sentences.en: But she's about to give it at NDC Tech Town.
sentences.zh: 但她马上要在 NDC Tech Town 上讲了。

sentences.en: Or I guess she's given by, now she has given it at NDC Tech Town.
sentences.zh: 或者说，我想现在她应该已经在 NDC Tech Town 上讲过了。

sentences.en: When I saw her, she was just about to leave for NDC Tech Town.
sentences.zh: 我见到她的时候，她正准备出发去 NDC Tech Town。

sentences.en: Yeah, that conference, I think, has just happened in, was it Kansberg in Norway?
sentences.zh: 是啊，那个会议我想应该刚在挪威的康斯贝格举行吧？

sentences.en: It is Kansberg in Norway, which is about an hour or so away from Oslo.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是挪威的康斯贝格，离奥斯陆大约一小时车程。

sentences.en: So I was considering going there for a day on my way out of Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时考虑过离开欧洲时顺道去那里待一天。

sentences.en: But I had to get back to Milan from the Czech Republic to fly back to New York.
sentences.zh: 但我必须从捷克回到米兰，才能飞回纽约。

sentences.en: And figuring out how to get from the Czech Republic to Kansberg and then from Kansberg to Milan was just too complicated for me.
sentences.zh: 而且要搞清楚怎么从捷克去康斯贝格，再从康斯贝格去米兰，对我来说太复杂了。

sentences.en: In Milan, is that where you were for your wedding stuff, if I recall correctly?
sentences.zh: 米兰，如果我没记错的话，那是你参加婚礼相关活动的地方吗？

sentences.en: Not a wedding.
sentences.zh: 不是婚礼。

sentences.en: No, just a family trip.
sentences.zh: 不，只是家庭旅行。

sentences.en: And no, we were in Tuscany.
sentences.zh: 而且不，我们是在托斯卡纳。

sentences.en: It was amazing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: We had a great time.
sentences.zh: 我们玩得很开心。

sentences.en: We stayed at this villa, this 15th century Medici villa that my stepfather had rented out to get the whole family together.
sentences.zh: 我们住在一栋 15 世纪的美第奇别墅里，是我继父租下来让全家人团聚的。

sentences.en: And it's a really cool tour company where they bring in all these, this, like, Italian chef who cooks for you for the whole week.
sentences.zh: 那是一家很酷的旅游公司，他们会请来各种人，比如一位意大利厨师，为你做整整一周的饭。

sentences.en: But, like, she's only a chef by night.
sentences.zh: 但她只有晚上才做厨师。

sentences.en: Her, like, her educational background is she has a PhD in geology.
sentences.zh: 她的教育背景是地质学博士。

sentences.en: And she's cooking you dinner every night.
sentences.zh: 而她每天晚上都给我们做晚餐。

sentences.en: And, like, one of the people who's the, like, the travel coordinator for this tour company has, like, a PhD in physics.
sentences.zh: 还有，这家旅游公司的旅行协调员之一，拥有物理学博士学位。

sentences.en: They're all, like, super smart and interesting people in addition to being, you know, great hosts and tour guides.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅是出色的东道主和导游，而且都是超级聪明、有趣的人。

sentences.en: So, we had, like, this very authentic, homey, Italian experience where we had home-cooked meals every day.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们体验了非常地道、温馨的意大利生活，每天都能吃到家常菜。

sentences.en: It was great and amazing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒、太神奇了。

sentences.en: And then I, then after that, I went to Czechia to spend a couple days hanging out with Hana.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我去了捷克，和 Hana 一起待了几天。

sentences.en: I spent a day in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 我在维也纳待了一天。

sentences.en: You and I spent a day in Vienna, but I spent a slightly longer day in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 你和我曾在维也纳待过一天，但我这次在维也纳待的时间稍微长一点。

sentences.en: Technically, I spent two hours and one day in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，我在维也纳待了一天零两个小时。

sentences.en: And then I spent, like, a full day in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 然后我又在维也纳待了完整的一天。

sentences.en: So, I spent, like, a day and a half in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在维也纳总共待了一天半。

sentences.en: And then I spent a day and a half in Milan.
sentences.zh: 然后我在米兰也待了一天半。

sentences.en: And then I came back.
sentences.zh: 之后我就回来了。

sentences.en: And I just got home.
sentences.zh: 我刚到家。

sentences.en: And now I'm trying to recover and get back into the swing of things.
sentences.zh: 现在我正试图恢复状态，重新步入正轨。

sentences.en: It's, like, the first vacation vacation I've taken in a while.
sentences.zh: 这算是我很久以来第一次真正的度假了。

sentences.en: I'm jealous you were in Milan.
sentences.zh: 我很嫉妒你在米兰。

sentences.en: Milan is on.
sentences.zh: 米兰正在进行时。

sentences.en: I was in Milan during Fashion Week.
sentences.zh: 我在时装周期间在米兰。

sentences.en: Like, I could care less about Fashion Week, what I care about.
sentences.zh: 我才不在乎什么时装周，我关心的是……

sentences.en: There were, there were, there were a lot of pretty girls at Fashion Week.
sentences.zh: 时装周上有很多漂亮的女孩。

sentences.en: Not, not.
sentences.zh: 不，不。

sentences.zh: 你确定 Ramona 现在不听这个播客吗？

sentences.zh: 嗯，Ramona 其实就在听力范围内。

sentences.en: So, I'm sure she heard that.
sentences.zh: 所以我肯定她听到了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 祝你好运。

sentences.en: Good luck to you.
sentences.zh: 也祝你好运。

sentences.en: But, I mean, we'll spend a whole episode on this.
sentences.zh: 不过，我的意思是，我们会花一整期节目来聊这个。

sentences.en: Because, listen, folks, we haven't actually mentioned this.
sentences.zh: 因为，听着，各位，我们还没提过这件事。

sentences.en: But this is the firSt.
sentences.zh: 但这是第一次。

sentences.en: Today is September 25th, 2023.
sentences.zh: 今天是 2023 年 9 月 25 日。

sentences.en: The last time you and I recorded, Bryce, sitting behind our computers was May 31St.
sentences.zh: Bryce，上次你我坐在电脑前录音还是 5 月 31 日。

sentences.en: That is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah, wow.
sentences.zh: 哇，天哪。

sentences.en: For almost exactly four months ago, minus a couple days.
sentences.zh: 几乎整整四个月前，只差几天。

sentences.en: We obviously recorded a bunch of times, potentially too many times, while we did our Slovenia 2023 road trip.
sentences.zh: 我们在 2023 年斯洛文尼亚公路旅行期间显然录了很多次，可能次数太多了。

sentences.en: Because it ended up, I don't actually have the exact count, but I think it was plus or minus like eight episodes.
sentences.zh: 因为最终，我没有确切的统计，但我觉得大概有八期左右。

sentences.en: And because we only do this weekly, that's one-sixth, 17% of our annual content.
sentences.zh: 而且因为我们每周只做一次，这占了我们年度内容的六分之一，即 17%。

sentences.en: And how have those episodes been received?
sentences.zh: 那些节目反响如何？

sentences.en: That's really the question.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正的问题。

sentences.en: That really answers whether it was too much, is whether they're doing well or not.
sentences.zh: 这才是判断是否过量的真正标准，看它们表现得好不好。

sentences.en: I think they're doing just as well.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们表现得一样好。

sentences.en: Honestly, I think at this point, I've been following the stats.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我觉得目前为止，我一直在关注数据。

sentences.en: We've kind of hit a...
sentences.zh: 我们似乎进入了一个……

sentences.en: Plateau.
sentences.zh: 平台期。

sentences.en: Well, I guess it's, yeah, a plateau.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想是的，一个平台期。

sentences.en: But that kind of sounds bad.
sentences.zh: 但这听起来有点糟糕。

sentences.en: We have advanced to our level of incompetence.
sentences.zh: 我们已经达到了我们的无能水平。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: It's like a thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个概念。

sentences.en: I'll find the reference.
sentences.zh: 我会找到出处的。

sentences.en: Yeah, find a link and we'll put it in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 好的，找到链接后我们把它放在节目说明里。

sentences.en: I'm confused.
sentences.zh: 我糊涂了。

sentences.en: But I think it's at this point, within, I think, a week or two, it's usually a couple thousand downloads, according to the site.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得目前为止，在一两周内，根据网站显示，通常会有几千次下载。

sentences.en: You know, who knows how accurate it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁知道它有多准确呢。

sentences.en: And then within a month or two, it peaks at about 3,000.
sentences.zh: 然后在一个月或两个月内，它会达到约 3000 次的峰值。

sentences.en: And I think that's been level for now half a year, a year or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个水平已经保持了半年、一年左右了。

sentences.en: So the reference is the Peter Principle, which is a concept in management developed by Lawrence J.
sentences.zh: 所以这个出处是“彼得原理”，这是由劳伦斯·J·彼得提出的管理学概念，

sentences.en: Peter, which observes that people in a hierarchy tend to rise to a level of respective incompetence.
sentences.zh: 它观察到等级制度中的人们往往会晋升到他们各自的无能水平。

sentences.en: So you get promoted based on your success in previous jobs until you reach a level at which you are no longer competent.
sentences.zh: 所以你会因为之前工作中的成功而获得晋升，直到你达到一个你不再胜任的水平。

sentences.en: And I think that applies here, too.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也适用于这里。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: We have become successful enough.
sentences.zh: 我们已经变得足够成功了。

sentences.en: We've gotten to a certain level where we now have an audience.
sentences.zh: 我们已经达到了一定水平，现在有了一定的听众。

sentences.en: And we're...
sentences.zh: 而且我们……

sentences.en: I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我不同意。

sentences.en: We're still...
sentences.zh: 我们仍然……

sentences.en: We may be at a temporary plateau, but I have great plans for the pod.
sentences.zh: 我们可能处于暂时的平台期，但我对这个播客有宏伟的计划。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the travel angle, the trip angle, I think, is really a fascinating thing that might take us to a whole new horizons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为旅行的角度，旅行的切入点，是一个非常迷人的东西，可能会带我们走向全新的视野。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I really do hope that the listeners are enjoying and being entertained by our antics on the road.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真心希望听众们能享受并被我们在路上的趣事所娱乐。

sentences.en: That being said, I mean, I have so much fun.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我的意思是，我玩得非常开心。

sentences.en: I mean, that three episode, which was just all one hour and a half bit when we were interviewing Sean at C++ on C,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那三期节目，就是我们在 C++ on Sea 采访 Sean 的那一个半小时的内容，

sentences.en: not only is that like one of the highlights of this podcast for me, that's like one of the highlights of my life.
sentences.zh: 那不仅是我在这个播客中的亮点之一，也是我人生中的亮点之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, that was a ton of fun.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: And honestly, so I looked at some of the comments on the interview that we just put in the last episode on Rob Leahy.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我看了我们在上一期采访 Rob Leahy 的评论。

sentences.en: Leahy?
sentences.zh: Leahy？

sentences.en: Rob, you're a dear friend of mine.
sentences.zh: Rob，你是我亲爱的朋友。

sentences.en: I hope you're not listening to this and to me butchering your name.
sentences.zh: 我希望你没在听这个，也没听到我把你的名字念得乱七八糟。

sentences.en: But we interviewed Rob in Venice, and there were two comments on Reddit, and both of them were like positive comments.
sentences.zh: 但我们在威尼斯采访了 Rob，Reddit 上有两条评论，而且都是正面评价。

sentences.en: And I was just like, wow, like we did a good job.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，哇，我们做得真不错。

sentences.en: And I haven't checked since, so nobody ruined it for me.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我就没再看过，所以没人能破坏我的好心情。

sentences.en: But like 100%, at the time I looked, it was 100% positive feedback.
sentences.zh: 但百分之百，在我看的时候，那是 100% 的正面反馈。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just like, oh, this is an okay episode.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是说“哦，这一期还行”。

sentences.en: It was like one of them was like amazing, and the other one was like unreal.
sentences.zh: 其中一条评价是“太棒了”，另一条是“不可思议”。

sentences.en: Wow, yeah, actually, I hadn't been keeping up with that.
sentences.zh: 哇，是啊，其实我一直没跟进那个。

sentences.en: That's good to hear.
sentences.zh: 听到这个真好。

sentences.en: I mean, that episode as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那一期也是。

sentences.en: I just honestly, it is some of those episodes.
sentences.zh: 老实说，确实是其中一些节目。

sentences.en: I mean, I always enjoy recording, but some of them where we're out and about interviewing people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我总是喜欢录音，但有些我们在外面采访人们的节目，

sentences.en: I think especially being at a conference, it's just you're around other passionate folks.
sentences.zh: 我觉得特别是在会议上，你周围都是充满激情的伙伴。

sentences.en: And anyways, it's just like I was going to say when you brought up NDC TechTown,
sentences.zh: 总之，就像我刚才在你提到 NDC TechTown 时想说的，

sentences.en: I was thinking we should correspond our conferences next year because I want to try and prioritize conferences that I haven't been to.
sentences.zh: 我在想我们明年应该协调一下参加的会议，因为我想优先考虑那些我还没去过的会议。

sentences.en: I know you've been to Core CPP.
sentences.zh: 我知道你去过 Core CPP。

sentences.en: Have you been to NDC TechTown?
sentences.zh: 你去过 NDC TechTown 吗？

sentences.en: I have not been to NDC TechTown.
sentences.zh: 我没去过 NDC TechTown。

sentences.en: I have not been to Core CPP.
sentences.zh: 我没去过 Core CPP。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is if we both go to the same conferences, we can do little, you know, interviewing speakers slash attendees.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，如果我们都去参加同一个会议，我们就可以做点小采访，你知道的，采访演讲者或者参会者。

sentences.en: I mean, we, I think historically have tended to focus on interviewing the speakers and podcast hosts like we did at C++ on C.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得我们过去往往倾向于采访演讲者和播客主持人，就像我们在 C++ on C 那样。

sentences.en: But I think it would be fun to like if we're giving out stickers, like we still don't have stickers yet, but we will have stickers in the future.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得如果能发贴纸会很有趣，虽然我们现在还没有贴纸，但以后会有。

sentences.en: And if we're giving them out, you know, just getting like little two minute, three minute, you know, sound bites from attendees that, you know,

sentences.en: You get these nodes that define streets and you want to generate a path that is kind of like a traveling salesman path, but you are trying to optimize.

sentences.en: But streets like in a graph, I would imagine are, are edges.

sentences.en: Nodes are basically like the minimal set of, I don't want to say intersections, but points that define the roads.

sentences.en: Okay.

sentences.en: That represent them.

sentences.en: And those represent everything like footpaths, bicycle paths, highways, residential areas.
sentences.zh: 它们代表了一切，比如人行道、自行车道、高速公路、住宅区。

sentences.en: And so a road is basically a highway or a way.
sentences.zh: 所以一条路基本上就是一条高速公路或一条“路”。

sentences.en: And a way is represented by a list of nodes in order.
sentences.zh: 而一条“路”是由一系列按顺序排列的节点表示的。

sentences.en: So if you've got a simple street that's just straight, it's probably just going to be two nodes.

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: One at the beginning, one at the end.

sentences.zh: 如果你有一条弯曲的街道，你最终会得到一堆节点，因为你必须用一堆基本上是直线的子组件来表示那条曲线。

sentences.en: So if you have a very curvy road, you're going to end up with like, you know, 50 nodes, even though it might be shorter than a straight street that has two nodes.

sentences.en: And so basically, you can build yourself a graph that represents the area you want to run.

sentences.zh: 那效率太低了。

sentences.zh: 所以你基本上想要一个“不落下任何节点”的算法，同时还要尽可能高效。

sentences.en: And that's the thing.

sentences.en: And exploring that, because then you just destroy your ability to make progress.
sentences.zh: 探索那个，因为那样你会破坏你取得进展的能力。

sentences.en: However, always going forward, if you're on, uh, basically a, a street where you're not at an intersection where you have options, isn't optimal.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你在一条基本上没有选择的街道上，一直向前走并不是最优的。

sentences.en: Because at some times, you want to basically just get a node that's like 10 meters in front of you.
sentences.zh: 因为有时，你基本上只想获得你前方 10 米处的一个节点。

sentences.en: But then the next node is like half a kilometer away, and as soon as you take that first step to the one that's 10 meters away,
sentences.zh: 但下一个节点在半公里之外，一旦你迈出第一步去往那个 10 米远的地方，

sentences.en: you then are forced to go half a kilometer to the next direction.
sentences.zh: 你就被迫向下一个方向走半公里。

sentences.en: So you basically want to have some, like what direction is forward?
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上想拥有一些，比如什么是“向前”的方向？

sentences.en: Direction when you're on a street that only has a node in front of you and a node behind you,
sentences.zh: 当你身处一条只有前方有一个节点、后方有一个节点的街道时，方向就是，

sentences.en: where there's basically no option other than keep going forward or reverse direction and go back where you came from.
sentences.zh: 除了继续向前或反转方向回到你来的地方之外，基本上没有其他选择。

sentences.en: What do you mean by direction?
sentences.zh: 你所说的“方向”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, you're running.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在跑步。

sentences.en: You're running.
sentences.zh: 你在跑步。

sentences.en: I'm a runner.
sentences.zh: 我是个跑者。

sentences.en: I'm running forward.
sentences.zh: 我在向前跑。

sentences.en: I understand.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: Most people run forward.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都是向前跑的。

sentences.en: I understand.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: There's no, there's no direction like north, east, west, south.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有所谓的北、东、西、南方向。

sentences.en: It's just, I'm running to the next node.
sentences.zh: 只是，我正跑向下一个节点。

sentences.en: But when I think about this problem, what I would imagine is that your position wouldn't have a particular orientation.
sentences.zh: 但当我思考这个问题时，我想象的是你的位置并没有特定的朝向。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So let me simplify this.
sentences.zh: 让我简化一下。

sentences.en: In general, you can think of when you're this algorithm or when you're running, you're in two different possible situations.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，你可以认为当你运行这个算法或者当你跑步时，你处于两种可能的情况中。

sentences.en: Situation one, you're at an intersection or you're at some place on a map where you have multiple options where you can go, you know, make a left-hand turn, right-hand turn,
sentences.zh: 第一种情况，你在一个十字路口，或者地图上的某个地方，你有多个选择，你知道，可以左转、右转，

sentences.en: you know, keep going forward.
sentences.zh: 你知道，继续向前走。

sentences.en: If you've got some stairs that you can go up, you know, you could have upwards of, you know, like 10, 11, 12 different directions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有楼梯可以上去，你知道，你可能会有超过，比如10、11、12个不同的方向。

sentences.en: But on average, you usually have like three or four.
sentences.zh: 但平均来说，你通常有三四个。

sentences.en: Or you are on a road where you can either, you technically do have two options.
sentences.zh: 或者你在一条路上，技术上你确实有两个选择。

sentences.en: You can continue to go the direction that you're currently going or you can turn around.
sentences.zh: 你可以继续沿着你当前的方向走，或者你可以掉头。

sentences.en: And as I mentioned before, you don't want to be in a situation where every single time you're going down this road in a direction, you're making a decision.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，你不想陷入那种每次沿着这条路走时都要做决定的情况。

sentences.en: Should I reverse direction or keep going forward?
sentences.zh: 我是该掉头还是继续向前？

sentences.en: If you're doing that every single time, you're going to completely destroy your ability to make progress in this algorithm.
sentences.zh: 如果你每次都这样做，你将彻底摧毁你在该算法中取得进展的能力。

sentences.en: So I have a threshold that says you're only allowed to backtrack if the next node in front of you is like further away above a certain distance.
sentences.zh: 所以我设定了一个阈值，规定只有当前方下一个节点距离超过一定距离时，才允许你折返。

sentences.en: I think on average I have that set to like 200 meters.
sentences.zh: 我想平均来说我把它设为200米左右。

sentences.en: So you're allowed to backtrack, like you're allowed to make the option to turn around in reverse direction.
sentences.zh: 所以你是被允许折返的，也就是说你可以选择掉头反向行驶。

sentences.en: If the next node on this street where you only have two options that's continuing to go forward and to go backward is greater than 200 meters.
sentences.zh: 如果这条街上只有两个选择，即继续向前和向后走，而下一个节点距离超过200米。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you have to keep going forward if it's only five meters away.
sentences.zh: 否则，如果它只有5米远，你就必须继续向前。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: When you talk about orientation, like is it assumed that you have some knowledge of where you came from and that therefore the or like you know I – okay.
sentences.zh: 当你谈到朝向时，是假设你知道自己从哪里来，因此……好吧。

sentences.en: Yes, you have a path.
sentences.zh: 是的，你有一条路径。

sentences.en: You have a path that is defined by a set of nodes and the node that is at the top of that path or the back of the path is where you just were.
sentences.zh: 你有一条由一组节点定义的路径，而位于该路径顶端或末端的节点就是你刚才所在的地方。

sentences.en: And so you can prevent yourself from revisiting that by checking the nodes that I'm about to explore are always going to contain the node that you just came from.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以通过检查即将探索的节点是否总是包含你刚来的那个节点，来防止自己重复访问。

sentences.en: And in certain situations, you want to make sure that you're not just always, you know, like I said,
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，你要确保自己不是总是，你知道，就像我说的，

sentences.en: destroying your ability to make progress because you only have a certain number of choices.
sentences.zh: 摧毁你取得进展的能力，因为你的选择数量有限。

sentences.en: Like I said, the steps that you make are really the choices that you make.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，你采取的步骤实际上就是你做出的选择。

sentences.en: So when you choose to take a left-hand turn or a right-hand turn or, you know, go across an intersection, that reduces your number of choices.
sentences.zh: 所以当你选择左转、右转，或者，你知道，穿过一个十字路口时，这会减少你的选择数量。

sentences.en: And if you're always including your ability to go backwards, I guess it's not going to make it impossible if you make progress.
sentences.zh: 如果你总是把向后走的能力也包括在内，我想这并不会让你无法取得进展。

sentences.en: But it's just – it explodes the dimensionality by like increasing, you know, the factor of N that your tree is growing out by every node gets N plus N.
sentences.zh: 但这只是——它会使维度爆炸，因为每增加一个节点，你的树就会以N的因子增长，每个节点都会变成N加N。

sentences.en: So I have a couple of logistical questions, light-hearted questions, humorous questions, color commentary.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一些后勤方面的问题，轻松点的问题，幽默的问题，还有花边评论。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I have some color commentary.
sentences.zh: 我有一些花边评论。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: So are you out there like running and then like you stop and you pull out your laptop and you type in where you need to go next?
sentences.zh: 所以你是跑着跑着停下来，拿出笔记本电脑，输入你接下来要去哪里吗？

sentences.en: I, 95% of the time while I run, have my cell phone in hand, screen turned on, and am looking at it like every 10 seconds.
sentences.zh: 我跑步时95%的时间都拿着手机，屏幕亮着，每10秒钟就看一眼。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And are running your algorithm?
sentences.zh: 你在运行你的算法吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: The algorithm is run in advance and generates the root.
sentences.zh: 算法是提前运行并生成路线的。

sentences.en: And the root is defined by a bunch of nodes that are latitude and longitude coordinates and you can just – I think it would have been funnier if you were building it as you go.
sentences.zh: 路线是由一堆经纬度坐标的节点定义的，你可以直接——我觉得如果你边跑边建路线会更有趣。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: I mean my roots are ridiculous though.
sentences.zh: 我是说我的路线很荒谬。

sentences.en: Like the number of 180-degree turns and the areas that it takes me.
sentences.zh: 比如180度转弯的数量，以及它带我去的那些区域。

sentences.en: Like when I was in Bangkok, there was this one – When were you in Bangkok?
sentences.zh: 比如我在曼谷的时候，有一次——你什么时候在曼谷的？

sentences.en: I was in Bangkok recently.
sentences.zh: 我最近去了曼谷。

sentences.en: My good friend, congratulations to Ethan and his partner, got married in Vietnam.
sentences.zh: 我的好朋友，恭喜Ethan和他的伴侣，在越南结婚了。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是吗。

sentences.en: You mentioned this to me.
sentences.zh: 你跟我提过。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so I was over in Southeast Asia and basically I was just running down a street and then ducking into these like 50-meter streets of which there were 28 of them.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在东南亚，基本上我就是沿着一条街跑，然后钻进这些50米长的小巷，总共有28条。

sentences.en: So in like a two-kilometer stretch, I completed 30 streets.
sentences.zh: 所以在两公里的路程里，我跑完了30条街。

sentences.en: And like on average, I would say the bare minimum, depending on what city you're in, you want like 10 streets per five kilometers.
sentences.zh: 平均来说，我觉得最起码，取决于你在哪个城市，你每五公里想要跑10条街。

sentences.en: But a good run, like my best run was 225 streets in 20 kilometers, which was –
sentences.zh: 但一次好的跑步，比如我最好的一次是20公里跑了225条街，那是——

sentences.en: Where was that?
sentences.zh: 那是在哪？

sentences.en: That was in Venice.
sentences.zh: 那是在威尼斯。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And which is why – this brings me back to Milan.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么——这让我想起了米兰。

sentences.en: I've also – I've been slowly – you know, the amount of data that you have – I got to tell you, I love Milan as a city, but the streets in Milan, absolutely terrible.
sentences.zh: 我也——我一直在慢慢地——你知道，你拥有的数据量——我得告诉你，我喜欢米兰这座城市，但米兰的街道，简直太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: I'll be running them.
sentences.zh: 我会跑完它们的。

sentences.en: All I care about –
sentences.zh: 我只关心——

sentences.en: All I care about is –
sentences.zh: 我只关心——

sentences.en: Seriously, it was like bad enough that I took like a scooter or like one of the e-bikes like once and I was like, I'm not doing this again.
sentences.zh: 说真的，糟糕到我曾经有一次骑了滑板车或电动自行车，当时我就想，我再也不要这样做了。

sentences.en: And then just like getting my luggage – like rolling my luggage the, you know,
sentences.zh: 还有就是拖着行李——拖着行李走，你知道，

sentences.en: five to 10 minutes between places I was staying in train stations was just such a hassle just because of the quality of the sidewalks and the streets.
sentences.zh: 在我住的地方和火车站之间那5到10分钟的路程，简直太麻烦了，全是因为人行道和街道的质量。

sentences.en: I mean, I loved everything about Italy, but Milan, you need to work on your streets.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我喜欢意大利的一切，但米兰，你们得改进一下街道。

sentences.en: Also, their curb cuts in Milan, like they have like a pretty noticeable bump on the curb cut,
sentences.zh: 还有，米兰的路缘坡道，它们在坡道上有一个相当明显的凸起，

sentences.en: which like if you're – you have some wheeled thing that you need to get onto or off the curb, having a big bump like sort of defeats the purpose of your curb cut.
sentences.zh: 这就像——如果你有带轮子的东西需要上下路缘，有个大凸起简直就失去了路缘坡道的意义。

sentences.en: But I have some other color commentary questions.
sentences.zh: 但我还有其他一些花边评论问题。

sentences.en: So how many times has this algorithm gotten you lost?
sentences.zh: 那么这个算法让你迷路过多少次？

sentences.en: Never.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: The –
sentences.zh: 那个——

sentences.en: Never?
sentences.zh: 从来没有？

sentences.en: The footnote on that answer is that I never get lost because I've got a phone in my hand with GPS.
sentences.zh: 那个答案的脚注是，我从不迷路，因为我手里拿着有GPS的手机。

sentences.en: However, I – it has told me to run places that it is not possible to run, probably the worst of which was once again when I was in Bangkok in Thailand.
sentences.zh: 然而，它确实告诉我去过一些根本不可能跑步的地方，最糟糕的一次大概又是当我在泰国曼谷的时候。

sentences.en: It wanted me to run onto a military compound and the men with guns at the entrance of this military compound.
sentences.zh: 它想让我跑进一个军事大院，而军事大院入口处有持枪的警卫。

sentences.en: I was – I clearly did not try to run in, but it was – It was apparent that when I got to that part of the map, I was taking a little detour.
sentences.zh: 我——我显然没有试图跑进去，但很明显——当我到达地图的那一部分时，我绕了一点路。

sentences.en: Well, and I was just about to ask, how sketchy of a – like have you built into your algorithm like the sketchiness of the neighborhoods?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我正要问，你有没有在算法里加入关于街区危险程度的考量？

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: I will say though, it is – Is this going to be what we're going to put on your tombstone?
sentences.zh: 不过我会说，这——这会成为我们要刻在你墓碑上的话吗？

sentences.en: It's like Connor was in some city and he ran into the bad neighborhood because the algorithm – the algorithm killed him.
sentences.zh: 就像Connor在某个城市，然后跑进了糟糕的街区，因为算法——算法杀了他。

sentences.en: It's not for the faint of heart though because a lot of the times you are running into a definitely like a residential street that is a dead end and people are staring at you being like,
sentences.zh: 不过这不适合胆小的人，因为很多时候你会跑进一条绝对是死胡同的住宅街，人们盯着你看，心想，

sentences.en: what are you doing running down my residential street?
sentences.zh: 你跑进我的住宅街是在干什么？

sentences.en: And then you kind of have to pretend that – or at least I do because I feel bad.
sentences.zh: 然后你得假装——或者至少我得这样做，因为我觉得很抱歉。

sentences.en: But like I'm looking for a way through and then I realize, oh, it's a dead end.
sentences.zh: 但我是在找路，然后我意识到，哦，这是个死胡同。

sentences.en: And then I – they kind of point to, you know, you got to go that way.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会指着，你知道，你得往那边走。

sentences.en: And I'm like, oh, thank you, thank you.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，谢谢，谢谢。

sentences.en: Especially for the ones where it's like, you know, it's a 20-meter street that I'm going just to complete because it's short.
sentences.zh: 特别是那些只有20米长的街道，我跑过去只是为了完成它，因为它很短。

sentences.en: So yeah, no sketchy neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，没有危险的街区。

sentences.en: There's been a couple streets that I've skipped though.
sentences.zh: 不过确实有几条街我跳过了。

sentences.en: Are you going to do this when we're in Nigeria?
sentences.zh: 我们在尼日利亚的时候你会这样做吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, why not?
sentences.zh: 是的，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Morocco?
sentences.zh: 摩洛哥？

sentences.en: I mean I think Morocco, they have rules though.
sentences.zh: 我是说我觉得摩洛哥，他们有规则。

sentences.en: Like you can't actually – I mean I'm not going to put my life on the line.
sentences.zh: 比如你不能真的——我是说我不会拿生命去冒险。

sentences.en: Well, I mean it actually depends on what the mortality rate would be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说这实际上取决于死亡率会是多少。

sentences.en: I'm not going to seriously put my life on the line.
sentences.zh: 我不会真的拿生命去冒险。

sentences.en: I mean I've been running next to highways that is probably not advised.
sentences.zh: 我是说我曾在高速公路旁边跑步，这可能是不被建议的。

sentences.en: I've definitely been running places that – and also I'm listening to my podcast while I'm doing it.
sentences.zh: 我确实在一些地方跑过——而且我跑步时还在听播客。

sentences.en: So I've got my headphones in and, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以我戴着耳机，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, so great situational awareness.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以情境感知能力真棒。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean but listen.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，但听着。

sentences.en: Listen, you got to have life goals.
sentences.zh: 听着，你得有生活目标。

sentences.en: And my current life goal is to be number one on this website.
sentences.zh: 而我目前的生活目标是成为这个网站的第一名。

sentences.en: And it's going to happen, folks.
sentences.zh: 这会实现的，伙计们。

sentences.en: This is – That is your current life goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是——这就是你目前的生活目标。

sentences.en: Well, look, I can't complain because my current life goals revolve around flying and spending money on ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 好吧，看，我没法抱怨，因为我目前的生活目标围绕着飞行和花钱在荒谬的事情上。

sentences.en: We all have the things that make us happy.
sentences.zh: 我们都有让我们快乐的事情。

sentences.en: Anyways, we're at the 43-minute mark.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们已经到了43分钟了。

sentences.en: We haven't even – this is a long episode.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没——这一集太长了。

sentences.en: So we got to – let's skip over to the two things I was going to mention.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得——让我们跳到我要提到的两件事上。

sentences.en: Episode 143, we mentioned R and we got a comment on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 第143集，我们提到了R，我们在Twitter上收到了一条评论。

sentences.en: Also, we're not calling it x.com.
sentences.zh: 另外，我们不会叫它x.com。

sentences.en: You know, maybe others will.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许别人会。

sentences.en: It's going to be Twitter.
sentences.zh: 它会是Twitter。

sentences.en: You know, I feel like not enough people are with us on this, but I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得没多少人跟我们站在一边，但我很抱歉。

sentences.en: You don't just get to rename a thing because you bought it.
sentences.zh: 你不能因为买下了一个东西就给它改名。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: Yeah, I heard that actually – I heard on another podcast today that Elon Musk has a biography.
sentences.zh: 是的，我听说实际上——我今天在另一个播客上听说Elon Musk有一本传记。

sentences.en: He already has a biography or – not autobiography but a biography written by Ashley Vance.
sentences.zh: 他已经有一本传记了，或者——不是自传，而是Ashley Vance写的传记。

sentences.en: Musk, terrible person, fired his secretary after 20 years.
sentences.zh: Musk，糟糕的人，在20年后解雇了他的秘书。

sentences.en: You know, anybody that looks up to him, you should go read his – go read Ashley Vance's book and –
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何崇拜他的人，都应该去读他的——去读Ashley Vance的书，然后——

sentences.en: but apparently Walter Isaacson, the individual behind the Steve Jobs biography and a couple other books, has written one about Elon Musk.
sentences.zh: 但显然Walter Isaacson，那个Steve Jobs传记和其他几本书背后的那个人，写了一本关于Elon Musk的书。

sentences.en: I will be consuming that ASAP.
sentences.zh: 我会尽快去读的。

sentences.en: Anyways, we're going to call this website Twitter because screw that guy.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们要把这个网站叫Twitter，因为去他的。

sentences.en: And until we get some, like, Gen Xers or whatever the young kids, you know, until they're asking us what is Twitter
sentences.zh: 直到我们得到一些，比如，X世代或者年轻的孩子们，你知道，直到他们问我们什么是Twitter，
